license_note: Motor rows: derived from thrustcurve-db 4.0.1 (ISC licence; github.com/broofa/thrustcurve-db, Robert Kieffer), which packages ThrustCurve.org motor data compiled by John Coker from manufacturer and certification-organisation submissions. Upstream diff from the same repository, main branch, fetched 2026-09-17 via raw.githubusercontent.com. Motor-mount tube and centering-ring dimensions in `supplement`: openrocket/openrocket-database component presets (Apache-2.0; Dave Cook, NAR 21953, and contributors), local copies at scratchpad/db/orc/*.orc; the numbers are vendor catalogue facts (LOC Precision, Madcow, Public Missiles, Always Ready Rocketry, Giant Leap, Estes) and are cited as such. Everything else in `supplement` is reviewer recall of vendor documents (Cesaroni Pro-X, AeroTech RMS, Loki Research, AMW, Aeropack) and carries no verified citation.

columns.key: unique row id = mfr|case (ThrustCurve manufacturerAbbrev | caseInfo)
columns.mfr: ThrustCurve manufacturerAbbrev of the RELOAD, i.e. the propellant vendor, not necessarily the case maker (see hardware_family)
columns.case: ThrustCurve caseInfo string, verbatim (hardware set name as entered)
columns.hardware_family: reconciler-normalised name of the physical case the row belongs to, for joining mis-vendored or interchangeable rows; CTI = Cesaroni Pro-X
columns.d_mm: ThrustCurve `diameter` field, mm: the NOMINAL motor class (18/24/29/32/38/54/75/98/152) in every row except Pro150 (161 = actual OD) and Loki/one ABC row (76 = 3.00 in class). NOT a measured case OD; see supplement case_od
columns.len_mm: LOADED motor length, mm: mode of the per-record ThrustCurve `length` values in the set (case + closures + nozzle as submitted); not the case-only length
columns.len_in: len_mm / 25.4 rounded to 3 decimals (conversion by reconciler; ThrustCurve stores mm, so no vendor inch figure exists to quote)
columns.len_variants: all distinct per-record length values in the set, mm, ascending; null when all records agree. Contains known typos (see disputed)
columns.total_g_min: minimum record totalWeightG in the set, g (loaded motor); null if no record has it
columns.total_g_max: maximum record totalWeightG in the set, g
columns.prop_g_max: maximum record propWeightG in the set, g
columns.classes: impulse letter classes present in the set, concatenated ascending
columns.motors: number of reload records in the set (thrustcurve-db 4.0.1)
columns.current: number of those records with availability == "regular" in 4.0.1 (stale; see current_upstream_main)
columns.current_upstream_main: same count computed from upstream thrustcurve-db main fetched 2026-09-17
columns.example: first record designation encountered in file order (not representative)
columns.records: all record designations in the set, for provenance
columns.confidence: certain / likely / recall as defined in notes (rows are never certain)
columns.source: derivation statement naming thrustcurve-db 4.0.1 and the grouping fields
columns.disputed: optional array: reviewer disagreements with {field, value, confidence, source, raised_by, evidence}; the row value itself is NOT changed

notes: PURPOSE AND LIMITS. This table answers "how long and how heavy is a loaded reload motor of a given hardware set" from ThrustCurve.org data. It does NOT contain any dimension a machined retainer, thrust ring, centering ring or MMT sleeve is designed to (case OD, case-only length, aft/forward closure OD, closure type, nozzle exit OD and protrusion, thread specs). Those live only in the `supplement` array and, apart from the MMT tube and centering-ring dimensions transcribed from the OpenRocket .orc files, every one of them is reviewer RECALL that was not verifiable here (vendor sites were unreachable). All three reviewers gave the same verdict: NOT FIT TO CUT METAL FROM until the club measures its own hardware. DOCTRINE (from the reviewers). (1) Measure the club's actual case with a micrometer (three readings) before any bore or press fit; treat all recalled case ODs as +/-0.15 to +/-0.5 mm. (2) Bore a machined MMT sleeve to the vendor MMT ID for that class (28.956 / 38.608 / 54.356 / 76.200 / 99.060 mm for LOC), not to case OD + 0.1; note the 29 mm class is a known snug fit and a 29.2-29.3 mm bore is advised.
